text:
Anaheim's hot scorer gets the headlines, but the Ducks' power play runs through Leo Carlsson. The 21-year-old center has 28 points in 23 games, 22 of them assists and 19 on the power play, at over 20 minutes a night. His ice time has crept up almost two more minutes over his last ten games.

Nothing about it looks borrowed. His goals match his expected goals (the quality of his chances), his teammates are only slightly ahead of theirs with him on, and last season Evolving-Hockey said he was better than his results: 2.4 expected wins against 1.1 actual. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 73% of his entries and in the 94th percentile of forwards for primary shot assists.

The gap is at five on five, where Anaheim gets 46.9% of the expected goals with him out there. NHL EDGE has him in the 99th percentile for skating bursts and distance, so the legs are there. Our talent range puts his true rate near 3.0 points per 60, a touch below his current 3.58. Watch the even-strength share.
